title: Memory leak when using `add_theme_font_size_override` repeatedly
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in 4.0.1-stable, 4.2.1-stable, 4..4.1-stable, and 4.5-dev2 ### System information Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) ### Issue description I've been trying to creating "responsive" UI system in Godot, part of which requires adjusting Label node's font size at runtime. To accomplish this, I've created a system that calls `self.add_theme_font_size_override(&"font_size", scaled_font_size)` when the game window changes size. However, I've noticed that every time this function is called, the Monitor tab in the Godot debugger shows that a little bit of memory is allocated and never released, indicating some kind of memory leak. I created a MRP that constantly increases the font_size override of a label, and the same problem occurs: I attempted to fix this by adding the following code before adding the override, but it unfortunately has no effect on memory: ``` if self.has_theme_font_size_override(&"font_size"): self.remove_theme_font_size_override(&"font_size") ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new project 2. Create a `2D`/`Control` scene 3. Add a `Label` node. 4. Attach a script to the label. 5. Create a `_process` function that calls `self.add_theme_font_size_override(&"font_size", x)`, where `x` is constantly changing. 6. Run the scene, and watch `Static Memory` and `Objects` in the Monitor within the Debugger ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [theme_override_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19658882/theme_override_test.zip)
